Toxic drool runs down the large amphibian's chin as it splashes in the marsh, the footing would be treacherous for most, but with wide clawed feet it is 
perfectly suited to the muddy bottoms and quickly traverses the bug-ridden Fenlands. A pang of hunger drives the simple minded creature onward as its 
forward facing eyes searches for the movement of something worth catching. Hoping to spot the unmistakably gangly silhouette of a freshwater bird, or 
the splash of a large fish but, instead, finds a curious cluster of brown furred rodents lazily float down the river. Its eyes widen in anticipation and two 
long tentacles, dripping in a yellowed slime, unfurl from its mouth as it bounds forward eager to lash the simple mammals into a toxic-laden stupor. 
Landing in the mud, its mouth agape and ready to attack, the four gurubara look up at the aggressive glomunder with half lidded eye. They sigh in 
unison and simply close their eyes once more. The breeze then picks up and the predator feels a gentle wave of calm, of satisfaction. Within moments its 
muscles relax, its pang of hunger subsides and it gently settles into the river. Hunting is exhausting, why not just rest for a moment...
Unlike a rolling expanse of trees, or a sky piercing mountain, the fresh waters of Sol’Kesh are not a single environment unto itself, but 
are instead a source of life that feeds the ecosystems it runs through. Every and all animals that live within the island rely on the Fenlands 
to a certain extent. A herd of rutort may meander into the Fenlands as they chew through river-coast-grown brookbuds, or a shaevrynn 
will swim through sunken woods to snare a fish. While many will enter the Fenlands to drink or hunt, there are some creatures that are 
so well adapted to these wet environments that they never leave. Freshwater fish swim through miles of river or flourish in land locked 
lakes. The larkiera and murrow dominate the gloomy waters, adapted perfectly to navigating the silt and plant choked waterways. Able 
to straddle both environments, amphibians thrive in the marshes and sunken forests like no other. Solmundis and glomunder terrorize 
the muddy riverbanks while fennfistle use their long legs to leap across the marshes in search of delectable bird eggs and, beneath them 
all, deep in the muck and mud of the lake bottoms, rests the monstrously large nuthorghull salamander. Once roused, the amphibian 
will consume any and all creatures that call their waters home. The Fenlands are truly a boisterous landscape with the buzzing of 
insects, untold number of frogs croaking their ballads and the bellowing of pebbleback auhk and baughur. These two megafauna, 
while content to happily wallow in the mud and chew through thick marsh grasses, can get rather territorial when the two herds find 
themselves encroaching on the same stretch of grass. When the two herds meet in such a manner, it's not long before the Fenlands are 
shaking with the body slams of the large mammals and eechoing, bellowing grunts that add only more noise to this riotious biome.
